subject: history_social
passage: In 1569, the Flemish mapmaker Gerardus Mercator published a world map designed for sailors. On his projection, a course that follows a single compass bearing appears as a straight line, so navigators could plot a route simply by drawing it with a ruler. That advantage came at a price. To keep compass directions true, the map stretches regions more and more as they get closer to the poles, so Greenland looks roughly as large as Africa, a continent about fourteen times its size.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain the purpose of a map's design and a distortion that came with it
choices.B: To describe how sailors found their way at sea before 1569
choices.C: To compare the actual sizes of Greenland and Africa
choices.D: To argue that Mercator's map should no longer be used for any purpose

explanation.why: The text first explains what Mercator's map was for: letting sailors plot a constant compass course as a straight line. "That advantage came at a price" then introduces the drawback, the growing stretch near the poles that makes Greenland look as large as Africa. The purpose covers both the design's benefit and its cost.
explanation.A: Correct. The text explains why the map was useful for navigation and then the size distortion that this design caused.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says nothing about navigation methods before Mercator's map.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Greenland and Africa are compared only as an example of the distortion; that comparison is a detail, not the main purpose.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text describes a drawback but never says the map should be abandoned, so this claims more than the text does.
